I made both edits in `src/flask/sansio/scaffold.py` as written. `patch` now calls `self.route(rule, methods=["PATCH"], **options)`, and the new `options_route` method sits directly after it and goes through `_method_route("OPTIONS", ...)`. I haven't run any tests.

One side effect: `patch` no longer gets the check in `_method_route` that raises `TypeError` when `methods` is passed. So `patch(rule, methods=[...])` will now fail with a different error, a duplicate keyword argument, instead of the clear message.

After the change, five methods call `_method_route` directly, all in `Scaffold`: `get`, `post`, `put`, `delete` and the new `options_route`. A search of `src/flask/` found no other direct callers. `patch` is no longer one of them.
